props.gloss_en: the baraita: the first waters -- one washes either with hot or with cold
the baraita: the final waters -- one washes only with cold
they taught [that the first waters may be hot] only where the hand does not recoil from them; but where the hand recoils, one does not wash with them
[on the final-waters clause:] they taught [only cold] only where the hand recoils; but where the hand does not recoil, one washes [with warm]
by implication, for the first waters, even where the hand recoils, it is permitted
the baraita: the middle waters are optional
Rav Nachman: they taught [that the middle waters are optional] only between one dish and another
Rav Nachman: but between a dish and cheese it is obligatory
the baraita: the final waters are an obligation
Rav Yehuda brei deR' Chiyya: why did they say the final waters are an obligation? because there is Sodomite salt, which blinds the eyes
Abaye: and it is found [in the proportion of] a pinch in a kor
Rav Acha brei deRava to Rav Ashi: what of all salt? -- [Rav Ashi:] it need not be said [that it requires the final waters]
Abaye: at first I would say that one does not wash the final waters onto the ground because of filth
the Master said to me: because an evil spirit rests upon them
Abaye: at first I would say that one does not take anything from the table when a person holds a cup to drink lest a mishap occur at the meal
the Master said to me: because it is bad for [a spirit of] tzerada
and we said this only where he takes and does not return it; taking and returning -- we have no [objection] to it
and we said this only beyond four cubits; within four cubits -- we have no [objection]
and we said this only of a thing the meal needs; a thing the meal does not need -- we have no [objection]
Mar bar Rav Ashi was particular even about the mortar and pestle for spices -- things the meal needs
Abaye: at first I would say that people gather crumbs for cleanliness
the Master said to me: because [leaving them] is bad for poverty

the tale: the prince of poverty pursued a man and could not overcome him, for he was very careful with crumbs; once he broke bread over grass, and after eating he uprooted the grass with a hoe and threw it into the river
the prince of poverty: now he has certainly fallen into my hand
the prince of poverty: woe, that man has driven me out of my house
Abaye: at first I would say that one does not drink foam because it is repulsive
the Master said to me: because it is bad for catarrh
blowing on it is bad for the head
pushing it away is bad for poverty
what is its remedy? to sink it in
for catarrh from wine -- beer
from beer -- water
from water -- it has no remedy; and this is what people say: poverty follows the poor
Abaye: at first I would say that one does not eat vegetables from a bundle the gardener tied because it looks like gluttony
the Master said to me: because it is bad for witchcraft
the tale: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna were travelling by boat; a matron asked to be seated with them and they refused; she said something and bound the boat; they said something and released it
the matron: what can I do to you, since you do not wipe yourselves with a shard, do not kill a louse on your garments, and do not eat vegetables from a bundle the gardener tied
Abaye: at first I would say that one does not eat vegetables that fell from the table because it is repulsive
the Master said to me: because it is bad for the breath of the mouth
Abaye: at first I would say that one does not sit under a gutter because of the waste water
the Master said to me: because demons are found there
the tale: porters carrying a barrel of wine set it down under a gutter to rest and it burst; they came before Mar bar Rav Ashi, who brought out horns and excommunicated [the demon]
the demon: how should I act, when they set it on my ear?
Mar bar Rav Ashi: what are you doing in a place where the many are found? you are the one who deviated -- go and pay!
the demon: anything tied, sealed, measured or counted, we have no authority to take from it until we find something ownerless
Abaye: at first I would say that one pours water from the mouth of the pitcher because of twigs
the Master said to me: because there are bad waters
the demon's son in Rav Pappa's house, sent for water and delayed: [I waited] until the bad waters passed
the demon's son, seeing them pour from the pitcher's mouth: had I known you are accustomed to do this, I would not have delayed
Rav Dimi: the first waters fed [someone] pig meat
Rav Dimi: the final waters took a woman from her husband
Ravin: the first waters fed [someone] carcass meat
Ravin: the final waters killed a soul
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: and your mnemonic -- Rav Dimi came and divorced her, Ravin came and killed her
R' Abba teaches one of these and one of those, the stricter
fire-heated water: Chizkiya -- one does not wash the hands from it
R' Yochanan -- one washes the hands from it
Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi (who ate taharot), asked by R' Yochanan: all the great men of the Galilee do so
the Tiberias springs: Chizkiya -- one does not wash the hands from them
Chizkiya -- but one immerses the hands in them
R' Yochanan -- the whole body immerses in them
R' Yochanan -- but not his face, hands and feet
Rav Pappa: in their place -- all agree it is permitted
Rav Pappa: taking from them in a vessel -- all agree it is forbidden
Rav Pappa: where they disagree is where one channelled them into a ditch
one master holds: we decree [against] the ditch on account of the vessel
and one master holds: we do not decree
the baraita: water unfit even for an animal to drink -- in vessels, it is unfit
the baraita: in the ground, it is fit
RSbE: even in the ground, one immerses the whole body in it
RSbE: but not his face, hands and feet
rather, is it not where one channelled them into a ditch, and they disagree on this
washing the hands for non-sacred food is on account of [the] usage [of] teruma
and also on account of a mitzva
Abaye: the mitzva to heed the words of the Sages
Rava: the mitzva to heed the words of R' Elazar ben Arakh
'and whomever the zav touches without having rinsed his hands in water' (Lev 15:11) -- R' Elazar ben Arakh: from here the Sages based the washing of the hands on the Torah
rather, this is what it says: and another who did not rinse [his hands] is impure
R' Oshaya: they spoke of washing the hands for fruit only on account of cleanliness
they understood from it: an obligation there is not, but a mitzva there is
Rava: neither obligation nor mitzva, but optional
Rav Nachman: one who washes his hands for fruit is nothing but one of the arrogant
Rabba bar bar Chana: I stood before R' Ami and R' Asi; a basket of fruit was brought, they ate and did not wash their hands, gave me nothing, and each blessed by himself
learn from it: there is no washing of the hands for fruit
and learn from it: one does not make a zimmun over fruit
and learn from it: two who ate -- it is a mitzva [for them] to separate
the baraita: two who ate -- it is a mitzva [for them] to separate
the baraita: when is this said? when both were scribes; but one a scribe and one ignorant -- the scribe blesses and the ignorant one fulfils [his obligation]
the baraita: washing the hands for non-sacred food -- until the joint
the baraita: for teruma -- until the joint
the baraita: sanctifying the hands and feet in the Temple -- until the joint
the baraita: anything that interposes in immersion of the body interposes in washing the hands for non-sacred food and in sanctifying hands and feet in the Temple
Rav: until here for non-sacred food [the nearer point]
Rav: until there for teruma [the farther point]
Shmuel: until here both for non-sacred food and for teruma -- stringently [non-sacred food]
Rav Sheshet: until here both for non-sacred food and for teruma -- leniently [teruma]
Rav: a person washes both his hands in the morning and stipulates upon them for the whole day
R' Avina to the people of Pakta deAravot: such as you, for whom water is not found -- wash your hands in the morning and stipulate upon them for the whole day
[R' Avina's ruling:] in a time of pressing need -- yes; not in a time of pressing need -- no
Rav Pappa: this irrigation channel [of the drawers] -- one does not wash the hands from it
Rav Pappa: for [its water] does not come by a man's force
Rav Pappa: and if he brings [his hands] near the bucket, where [the water] comes by a man's force -- one washes from it
Rav Pappa: and if the bucket is pierced [with a hole] that admits liquid, [the waters] are joined, and one immerses the hands in it
Rava: a vessel pierced [with a hole] that admits liquid -- one does not wash the hands from it
Rava: a vessel that does not have a quarter-log in it -- one does not wash the hands from it
Rava: a vessel that cannot hold a quarter-log -- one does not wash the hands from it
hence one that holds [a quarter-log] -- [one washes] even though it does not have it in it
this [ruling, 'has a quarter-log in it'] is for one [person]
that [ruling, 'can hold a quarter-log'] is for two
the baraita: with a quarter-log of water one washes the hands for one, and even for two
are you particular about the vessel? -- yes
about the appearance [of the water]? -- yes
about the measure? -- yes
[version 2] about the measure we are not particular
Rav Yaakov of Nehar Pekod fashioned a washing-cup holding a quarter-log
Rav Ashi in Hutzal fashioned a jug holding a quarter-log
Rava: a barrel-stopper that one fitted -- one washes the hands from it
the baraita: a barrel-stopper that one fitted -- one washes the hands from it
the baraita: a skin-bottle and a kefisha that one fitted -- one washes from them
the baraita: a sack and a basket, even though they hold [water] -- one does not wash from them
the mishna: when they gave R' Tzadok less than an egg-bulk of food, he took it in a cloth, ate it outside the sukka, and did not bless after it
is it not: hence an egg-bulk requires washing the hands [even with a cloth]?
Shmuel found Rav eating with a cloth and said to him: do we act so? he said to him: my mind is short with me
Rav: my mind is short with me [the reason I eat with a cloth]
R' Zeira to R' Ami and R' Asi, found eating with worn skins: two great men like you -- should you err about Rav and Shmuel? he said 'my mind is short with me'!
R' Zeira: R' Ami and R' Asi err [in eating with worn skins]
Shmuel: they permitted a cloth to those who eat teruma
Shmuel: and they did not permit a cloth to those who eat taharot
and R' Ami and R' Asi were priests
one who eats by another's feeding requires washing the hands
one who eats by another's feeding does not require washing the hands
Rav Huna bar Sechora stood before Rav Hamnuna, put a piece of meat in his mouth and he ate; he said to him: were you not Rav Hamnuna, I would not feed you
Rav: a person should not put a slice into the attendant's mouth unless he knows that he washed his hands
Rav: and the attendant blesses over each and every cup
Rav: and he does not bless over each and every slice
R' Yochanan: he blesses over each and every slice
Rav Pappa: this [Rav's] is where there is an important person
Rav Pappa: that [R' Yochanan's] is where there is no important person
the baraita: a person should not give a slice to the attendant, whether the cup is in his hand or in the host's hand, lest a mishap occur at the meal
the baraita: an attendant who did not wash his hands -- it is forbidden to put a slice into his mouth
one who feeds [another] requires washing the hands
one who feeds [another] does not require washing the hands
RSbG: a woman rinses one hand in water and gives bread to her small son
they said of Shammai the Elder that he did not want to feed with one hand, and they decreed upon him that he feed with both his hands
Abaye: there, it is because of Shivta

Shmuel's father found Shmuel crying: my teacher struck me, for he said: you feed my son and did not wash your hands. -- And why did you not wash? -- he eats, and I should wash?! -- his father: is it not enough that he did not learn, he strikes as well!

שאין מחזיק -- הא מחזיק, אף על גב דלית ביה
דתניא: מי רביעית נוטלין לידים לאחד ואפילו לשנים
[איכא דאמרי] דתניא: מי רביעית נוטלין לידים לאחד ואפילו לשנים -- the quarter-log need not be per person

deflected_by.gloss_en: ולא היא, שאני התם משום דקאתו משירי טהרה -- there the water is the remnant of a measure that was once sufficient

supports.gloss_en: תניא נמי הכי: מגופת חבית שתקנה נוטלין ממנה לידים
תא שמע: נטלו במפה... מאי לאו -- הא כביצה בעי נטילת ידים

deflected_by.gloss_en: דלמא הא כביצה בעי סוכה ובעי ברכה -- the inference from less-than-an-egg-bulk concerns the sukka and the blessing, not the washing

supports.gloss_en: תא שמע: שמואל אשכחיה לרב דקאכיל במפה, אמר ליה: עבדין כדין? אמר ליה: דעתי קצרה עלי -- the text does not spell out the inference; R' Zeira reads it at 107b.2
מאי טעמא, לאו משום דזהיר ולא נגע?

deflected_by.gloss_en: לא, דזריז קדים ומשי ידיה מעיקרא -- he was diligent and had washed beforehand

supports.gloss_en: מכל מקום הא קאמר: אלא אם כן יודע שנטל ידיו -- the one fed must have washed

deflected_by.gloss_en: שאני שמש דטריד -- an attendant is different, for he is busy

supports.gloss_en: תא שמע: אשה מדיחה את ידה אחת במים ונותנת פת לבנה קטן... וגזרו עליו שיאכיל בשתי ידיו -- the feeder washes

deflected_by.gloss_en: התם משום שיבתא -- there it is because of Shivta, not because of feeding

supports.gloss_en: תא שמע: ...לא מיסתייה דלא גמיר, מימחא נמי מחי -- the feeder need not wash

objections.gloss_en: השתא כל גופו טובל בהם, פניו ידיו ורגליו לא כל שכן? -- if the whole body may immerse, how can the hands not?

answered_by.gloss_en: in place all permit; drawn in a vessel all forbid; they differ where it was channelled into a ditch -- one decrees ditch on account of vessel, one does not (= p_rp_machloket_bat_birta)

objections.gloss_en: השתא כל גופו טובל בהן, ידיו ורגליו לא כל שכן?

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא לאו דפסקינהו בבת בירתא, ובהא פליגי (= p_machloket_tannaim_bat_birta)

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה רבא לרב נחמן: מאי משמע? ... הא שטף טהור? הא טבילה בעי! -- the verse cannot mean that a zav who rinses his hands is pure, for he requires immersion

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא הכי קאמר: ואחר שלא שטף טמא -- the verse speaks of another person who did not rinse (= p_acher_shelo_shataf_tamei)

objections.gloss_en: איני? והאמר רבא: כלי שאין מחזיק רביעית אין נוטלין ממנו, הא מחזיק אף על גב דלית ביה -- an amoraic-memra contradiction (no ObjectionKind of its own)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא לחד, הא לתרי (= p_ha_lechad, p_ha_litrei)

objections.gloss_en: אשתמיטתיה הא דאמר רב תחליפא בר אבימי אמר שמואל: התירו מפה לאוכלי תרומה... ורבי אמי ורבי אסי כהנים הוו -- it escaped R' Zeira that the cloth is permitted to teruma eaters, and they were priests
Rav: the attendant does not bless each slice; R' Yochanan: he does

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא דאיכא אדם חשוב, הא דליכא אדם חשוב (= p_rp_ika_adam_chashuv, p_rp_leika_adam_chashuv)
